headline: ICT 30 accused, including Sheikh Hasina, ordered to surrender
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has ordered newspaper notices to be published to call for the surrender of 30 fugitives in the 2013 Shapla Chattar killings case.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has ordered the publication of notices in newspapers to call for the surrender of 30 fugitives, including ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and former Army Chief General Aziz Ahmed.
The order comes in connection with a case regarding crimes against humanity in the killings during the May 5, 2013, Hefazat-e-Islam rally at Motijheel's Shapla Chattar in Dhaka.
A total of 41 people are accused in the case. While 30 remain fugitives, 11 others are already in custody and were produced before the tribunal on Thursday.
Other high-profile fugitives ordered to surrender include former Home Minister Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, former Foreign Minister Hassan Mahmud, and former IGP Benazir Ahmed.
The tribunal has directed that notices be published in one Bengali and one English daily newspaper before the next hearing date, September 20.
Among those already in custody and produced in court include former ministers Abdul Latif Siddiqui, Hasanul Haq Inu, and Dipu Moni.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina and 29 others ordered to surrender by the ICT in the Shapla Chattar killings case.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has ordered the publication of notices in newspapers to call for the surrender of 30 fugitives, including ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and former Army Chief General Aziz Ahmed.

The order comes in connection with a case regarding crimes against humanity in the killings during the May 5, 2013, Hefazat-e-Islam rally at Motijheel's Shapla Chattar in Dhaka.

A total of 41 people are accused in the case. While 30 remain fugitives, 11 others are already in custody and were produced before the tribunal on Thursday.

Other high-profile fugitives ordered to surrender include former Home Minister Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, former Foreign Minister Hassan Mahmud, and former IGP Benazir Ahmed.

The tribunal has directed that notices be published in one Bengali and one English daily newspaper before the next hearing date, September 20.

Among those already in custody and produced in court include former ministers Abdul Latif Siddiqui, Hasanul Haq Inu, and Dipu Moni.

headline_marked: ACC [[launches probe against Asif Mahmud]] and 3 officials over corruption
headline: ACC launches probe against Asif Mahmud and 3 officials over corruption
summary: Former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan is the first such adviser to face an anti-corruption inquiry regarding irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has launched an investigation into alleged corruption and irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, naming four officials, including former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan.
The probe follows a complaint alleging a syndicate handled tendering and procurement, as well as corruption in recruitment, promotions, appointments, and transfers.
Specific allegations include the taking of Tk 76 lakh to transfer 38 upazila youth development officers, Tk 1.5 crore for promoting 150 assistant officers, and Tk 2 crore for preferred postings.
Other officials under investigation include former ministry secretary Md Mahbub-ul-Alam, former joint secretary Sheikh Mohammad Zobayer Hossain, and deputy secretary Md Masum Ahmed.
Asif Mahmud, now spokesperson of the National Citizen Party, has denied all allegations, calling them politically motivated.
He has given the ACC a 24-hour ultimatum to apologize for defaming him, warning that he will serve a legal notice if they fail to do so.
Despite the ultimatum, Asif stated he is ready to cooperate with any lawful inquiry and provide all necessary documents.
caption:
First former interim adviser under fire: ACC probes Asif Mahmud over alleged multi-crore corruption in the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has launched an investigation into alleged corruption and irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, naming four officials, including former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan.

The probe follows a complaint alleging a syndicate handled tendering and procurement, as well as corruption in recruitment, promotions, appointments, and transfers.

Specific allegations include the taking of Tk 76 lakh to transfer 38 upazila youth development officers, Tk 1.5 crore for promoting 150 assistant officers, and Tk 2 crore for preferred postings.

Other officials under investigation include former ministry secretary Md Mahbub-ul-Alam, former joint secretary Sheikh Mohammad Zobayer Hossain, and deputy secretary Md Masum Ahmed.

Asif Mahmud, now spokesperson of the National Citizen Party, has denied all allegations, calling them politically motivated.

He has given the ACC a 24-hour ultimatum to apologize for defaming him, warning that he will serve a legal notice if they fail to do so.

Despite the ultimatum, Asif stated he is ready to cooperate with any lawful inquiry and provide all necessary documents.
